title: Creality Scan 4.3.2 crashes during 3D calibration on pre-Haswell CPUs (BMI1 / #UD)
originalText:
Creality Scan 4.3.2 crashes during 3D calibration on pre-Haswell CPUs (BMI1 / #UD )
TL;DR: 4.3.2 ships native plugins compiled for Haswell+. On my Ivy Bridge-E Xeon the calibration computes fine (score 98.1) and then the app dies with STATUS_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION on an ANDN instruction. No error dialog, no event log entry, result is lost. 3/3 attempts.
What happens
Connect CR-Scan Raptor, run Calibrate , capture all 20 poses.
Progress reaches “computing calibration result”.
App closes by itself ~2 s later. No error, no dialog. Next launch says “Previous application crashed” .
Wasted three full calibration runs this way.
Why
Exception: 0xC000001D = STATUS_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION ( #UD )
Module: line_laser_param_preprocessing.dll at RVA 0x11348
Instruction: andn ecx, r10d, ebx
ANDN is BMI1 , introduced with Haswell (2013) . My CPU doesn’t have BMI1, so the opcode is invalid and the process is killed. The DLL has 28 ANDN instructions , all in the same TEA-style block decryption routine.
The calibration itself succeeds — the native log shows score 98.14 , rms fine — then dies in the [Line Trans] stage right after refresh_linelaser_params() . So the scanner, board and algorithm are all fine. …

title: Is there a way to get really small movements of an item in Creality slicer?
originalText:
The smallest movement I get using the shift-arrow keys is about twice as large as I need to line up items to be assembled.
Thanks!
I’m assuming you are referring to the (M)ove command. Theses are the Keyboard commands
Arrow keys = move selected object 10 mm
Shift + Arrow key = move selected object 1 mm
Ctrl + Arrow key = move relative to the camera orientation , rather than the bed X/Y axes.
However, for finer movements it’s generally accepted that the harrow handles and/or position fields are best for finer movements. You can dial in up to 0.01mm precision by typing in the precise movement you want.

title: Creality 7.2: interior corners at convex "stepped" shapes not solid
originalText:
I’ve been having an issue with Creality Print for a long time now. I’ve reported this on reddit like last year but it still persists.
Basically, whenever I print something with “stepped” structures (a vertical wall meets a horizontal floor/ceiling at a perfect 90degree angle), the corner where the two sides meet always ends up being a point of failure, as it doesn’t properly place solid material there. The vertical wall ends, there’s a single layer in the horizontal structure that overlaps it, and the rest of the horizontal structure starts at the vertical wall’s outer surface.
In basically every case I’ve dealt with thus far, this has resulted in the vertical structure having an incredibly weak connection to the horizontal one, being essentially held together by a few wall-widths of bottom surface layer, and sparse infill. Especially in the case of objects with “shafts” which are completely embedded within horizontal surfaces, this results in “shafts” which break off incredibly easily, due to a lack of solid structural connection/support, and we’ve had to waste a lot of effort designing around this problem.

originalText:
Hi Creality community and support team,
I wanted to share an issue I’ve been facing for a while with my CR-M4 printer and that I finally managed to understand and resolve on my own.
I was experiencing persistent problems with print interruptions — both during planned filament changes and after unexpected power outages. The printer was simply not resuming or detecting the runout, which was extremely frustrating on long prints.
After testing across multiple versions of Creality Print (including the most recent ones available for Mac Intel chip), I discovered that none of them include the necessary G-code commands to activate these features by default in the machine start profile for the CR-M4.
Specifically, the following commands were completely absent from the Machine Start G-code:
M413 S1 ; Enable Power Loss Recovery
M412 S1 ; Enable Filament Runout Sensor
M500 ; Save settings to EEPROM
The CR-M4 firmware does support these features — the problem is purely that the slicer profile never activates them. As a workaround, I had to add these lines manually to the Machine Start G-code in Creality Print’s printer settings. …

title: [SOLVED] K1C Firmware 1.3.5.22 - Internal Camera Working Again in Mainsail/Fluidd
originalText:
After spending several hours troubleshooting this together with ChatGPT, I finally found a solution that works on my K1C running firmware 1.3.5.22 with the new camera hardware .
I hope this saves someone else a lot of time.
Symptoms
After updating to 1.3.5.22 :
Camera still works in Creality Print
AI detection still works
Camera disappears from Mainsail/Fluidd
Camera Settings Control cannot be installed (“not compatible with the new hardware version”)
/webcam/?action=stream no longer works
No mjpg_streamer service is running
What I found
The firmware no longer streams directly from the UVC device.
Instead, Creality uses:
cam_app
which writes camera frames into shared memory:
/dev/shm/camera_main
The existing input_uvc.so method is no longer usable.
Trying to start MJPG Streamer with input_uvc.so results in:
undefined symbol: parse_resolution_opt
The correct plugin is actually:
input_memfd.so

title: OrcaSlicer 2.4.1 — K2 Pro CFS + Device Control Findings
originalText:
For anyone running OrcaSlicer 2.4.1 with a K2 Pro, here’s what I’ve found on connection methods and what actually works.
The Setup That Works
Host Type: CrealityPrint
Printer Agent: CrealityPrint
Hostname: 192.168.1.xx:4408 (your printer’s IP + port 4408)
See screenshot below.
What You Get
Device control through OrcaSlicer — printer status, temps, print management — all functional
CFS filament slots visible and manageable
Prints send and run without issue
What You Don’t Get
Camera — the K2 Pro uses WebRTC architecture that OrcaSlicer cannot access regardless of connection method. This is a hardware/firmware limitation, not an OrcaSlicer issue.
Background
Prior to 2.4.x the only working OrcaSlicer path was Octo/Klipper at :4408, which gave device control but no CFS sync. The CrealityPrint host type added in 2.4.x adds CFS sync — and using :4408 in the hostname field is what restores device control alongside it.
Camera remains the outstanding limitation. If anyone has found a workaround post below.

title: Creality Print 7.2 PETG Temperature Bug Confirmed by Support
originalText:
Just a heads-up for anyone using Creality Print 7.2 with PETG, especially eSUN PETG.
After updating from Creality Print 7.1 to 7.2, my PETG filament profiles were affected. The recommended nozzle temperature range still looked normal, but the actual first-layer and other-layer print temperatures were changed to 200°C. Because of this, the printer could not extrude PETG properly.
On the Creality K2 Plus itself, the filament still showed eSUN PETG with the correct range of around 230°C to 260°C, so the issue seems to be with the slicer/software profile after the update.
I contacted Creality support, and they confirmed that this is a bug in the latest software version. Their advice was to uninstall the current version and install an older version of Creality Print. They specifically suggested trying version 7.1.1.4472_Release while their software team works on the bug.
For now, before printing PETG in Creality Print 7.2, double-check your filament profile and make sure the actual print temperature is correct, not just the displayed recommended range.

title: The light off delay on Halot R6 is either bugged, or if it is working in the intented way, it is useless.
originalText: On the Halot R6, the light-off delay happens before the build plate lifts, while the cured layer is still pressed against the FEP. This is the opposite of how most resin printers work, where the delay happens after lifting, letting the resin settle and suction release more smoothly. Because of this, increasing light-off delay on the R6 just makes the print sit stuck to the FEP longer, which actually increases adhesion and makes peeling harder. This is especially a problem with viscous or tough resins. It’s likely a firmware issue, but it makes dialing in settings way more difficult than it should be. The problem could be resolved by setting the lifting height heigher, but the device limits it at 5 mm, which is not enough.

I. What is a .3MF File?
The .3MF (3D Manufacturing Format) is an open standard file format specifically designed for 3D printing. Its purpose is to provide a unified and efficient way to represent various aspects of 3D models, including geometry, color, texture, and material properties. This facilitates seamless transfer and printing across different 3D design software, slicing software, and 3D printers. Compared to other formats, the .3MF format offers enhanced compatibility and a richer set of features.II.
II. Advantages of the 3MF File Format
Richness: While the STL format is widely used, it lacks information regarding color and material properties. In contrast, the .3MF format includes comprehensive data on geometry, color, materials, and copyright information.
